about: The epistola of the formulary “Third Sunday after Easter” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Dearly beloved: I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul. Keep your conduct good among the Gentiles, that whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by considering your good works, glorify God in the day of visitation. Be ye subject therefore to every human creature for God’s sake: whether to the king as pre-eminent, or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of the good. For so is the will of God, that by doing well you may silence the ignorance of foolish men. As free men, and not as having liberty for a cloak of malice, but as servants of God. Honor all men; love the brotherhood; fear God; honor the king. Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh. For this is grace in Christ Jesus our Lord.

ex.w021: The participle describes the readers Peter addresses. It stands in the nominative, although the sentence names them only by the accusative “vos”. No separate word expresses its subject, an understood you.
